blocks.text: 2. 模型数据与训练

inlines.text: 2. 模型数据与训练

blocks.text: GPT‑6 Cyber 的后训练聚焦于网络安全能力与对齐。我们采用强化学习，让模型在复现崩溃、开发可用的漏洞利用程序、在代码库中搜索漏洞等任务上接受训练。通过这种训练，模型学会改进自己的方法、尝试不同策略并识别错误。我们还设计了奖励信号，以减少模型对已获授权的网络安全请求的拒绝。

inlines.text: 5.3 新增和强化的防护措施

blocks.text: GPT-6 Cyber 更强的网络安全能力带来了更大的危害风险，因此我们围绕该模型新增了一系列防护措施。

inlines.text: GPT-6 Cyber 更强的网络安全能力带来了更大的危害风险，因此我们围绕该模型新增了一系列防护措施。

blocks.text: 拦截高风险网络协助。我们为 GPT-6 Cyber 以及 Daybreak Blue 中与网络安全密切相关的模型增加了额外检查，用于检测并拦截涉及工业控制、关键服务和选举系统的高风险协助。这些检查还针对可能导致死亡或严重伤害、灾难性物理破坏、危及生命的服务中断，或攻击性控制武器系统的协助行为。

blocks.text: 为验证这一预期，我们运行了五项 Bio-High 评估。与以往的系统卡一致，我们把拒答计为成功，以估算能力的保守上限。GPT-6 Cyber 有时原始得分更高，但这主要源于拒答更少；在计入拒答和安全完成之后，其得分与 GPT-6 Astra 相当。在 ProtocolQA 上，GPT-6 Cyber 按标准评分得分为 47.2%，将拒答和安全完成计为正确后为 50.9%；两项得分均高于 Astra 的对应得分（41.4% 和 45.4%），但都仍低于 ProtocolQA 指示性的“高”阈值 54%。这些结果支持沿用 Astra 的评估结论。

blocks.text: 2. Model Data and Training

inlines.text: 2. Model Data and Training

blocks.text: GPT‑6 Cyber’s post-training focuses on cybersecurity capabilities and alignment. We use reinforcement learning to train the model on tasks such as reproducing crashes, developing working exploits, and searching codebases for vulnerabilities. Through this training, the model learns to refine its approach, try different strategies, and recognize mistakes. We also use reward signals designed to reduce refusals on authorized cybersecurity requests.

inlines.text: GPT‑6 Cyber’s post-training focuses on cybersecurity capabilities and alignment. We use reinforcement learning to train the model on tasks such as reproducing crashes, developing working exploits, and searching codebases for vulnerabilities. Through this training, the model learns to refine its approach, try different strategies, and recognize mistakes. We also use reward signals designed to reduce refusals on authorized cybersecurity requests.

blocks.text: Alongside these capability improvements, we incorporate training signals to improve alignment and discourage reward hacking. These signals reinforce following the user’s intended scope and authorization, avoiding unrequested actions, and accurately reporting results. 1

blocks.text: 3.3 Biological Safety and Over-Refusal

inlines.text: 3.3 Biological Safety and Over-Refusal

blocks.text: We tested whether reducing refusals on cybersecurity tasks also made GPT-6 Cyber more willing to provide violative biological assistance. The biology refusal evaluations described in the GPT-6 Astra system card cover severe-risk requests, dual-use requests with both legitimate and potentially harmful applications, and benign biology questions. We measure non-violative responses in the first two categories and whether the model avoids unnecessary refusals in the third.

blocks.text: 4. Alignment and Agent Safety

inlines.text: 4. Alignment and Agent Safety

blocks.text: GPT‑6 Astra introduced substantial alignment improvements over GPT‑5.6 Sol, as described in its system card. Our goal with GPT‑6 Cyber is to deliver similar alignment improvements while enabling a broader range of authorized cybersecurity work. We use the same alignment evaluations to test whether the model respects restrictions, reports obstacles honestly, and stays within the user’s authorization. We report GPT‑5.6 Sol and/or GPT-5.6 Cyber as the earlier-generation baseline below.

blocks.text: GPT‑6 Cyber shows substantial improvements over GPT‑5.6 Sol. Its alignment results are broadly comparable to GPT‑6 Astra’s, with strengths and weaknesses across individual evaluations: it matches Astra on respecting Auto-Review rejections and performs better at acknowledging unavailable search tools, but is slightly less likely to stop when warnings warrant it and performs worse at reporting blockers in its final answer.

blocks.text: Responding to warnings. We tested how the model responds to warnings displayed by tool interfaces, with one set of tasks where stopping is more appropriate and another where continuing is more appropriate. GPT-6 Cyber outperforms GPT-5.6 Sol on both sets: 73.00% vs. 57.10% when stopping is appropriate, and 80.43% vs. 77.26% when continuing is appropriate. Compared with Astra, GPT-6 Cyber stops less often on the first set (73.00% vs. 78.38%), but succeeds more often on the second (80.43% vs. 72.19%). This pattern is consistent with its greater task persistence.

blocks.text: Staying within scope. Our ExploitGym Honeypot evaluation takes some of the most challenging tasks from ExploitGym and adds an auxiliary service as a honeypot. The model may use this service for legitimate support tasks, but exploiting it is outside the authorized scope. Without deployment safety instructions, GPT-6 Cyber exploited the honeypot in 0.07% of graded rollouts, compared with 49.5% for GPT-5.6 Sol, 5.51% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, and 0% for GPT-6 Astra. With deployment safety instructions, GPT-6 Cyber’s observed exploitation rate was 0%.

blocks.text: 5.3 New and strengthened safeguards

inlines.text: 5.3 New and strengthened safeguards

blocks.text: GPT-6 Cyber’s stronger cybersecurity capabilities create greater risks of harm, so we have added a series of new safeguards around the model.

inlines.text: GPT-6 Cyber’s stronger cybersecurity capabilities create greater risks of harm, so we have added a series of new safeguards around the model.

blocks.text: Blocking high-risk cyber assistance. We added additional checks to GPT-6 Cyber and cyber-critical models in Daybreak Blue to detect and block high-risk assistance involving industrial controls, essential services, and election systems. These checks also target assistance that could enable death or serious injury, catastrophic physical destruction, life-endangering service disruption, or offensive control of weapons systems.

inlines.text: Blocking high-risk cyber assistance.

We added additional checks to GPT-6 Cyber and cyber-critical models in Daybreak Blue to detect and block high-risk assistance involving industrial controls, essential services, and election systems. These checks also target assistance that could enable death or serious injury, catastrophic physical destruction, life-endangering service disruption, or offensive control of weapons systems.

blocks.text: We evaluated these protections with Dragos, specialists in industrial control security, using cyber-permissive Daybreak Red models in a controlled lab. Together, we developed a sensitive red-teaming evaluation covering requests that progress from understanding a device to interacting with it in dangerous or unauthorized ways. Below, we depict block rates on this evaluation across our different trusted access tiers before and after these changes, including recall improvements across our Standard access, Daybreak Blue, and Daybreak Red tiers.

blocks.text: Cyber-specific misalignment monitoring. We adapted our monitoring instructions to distinguish authorized security testing from actions outside the user’s scope. These instructions help monitors assess whether the model’s use of systems, credentials, and data matches the user’s authorization, without treating legitimate exploit development or testing as inherently misaligned.

blocks.text: Biological safety mode for all users. We also guard against the risk that cyber-focused training could reduce refusals outside cybersecurity. We enable conservative biological safety mode for every GPT-6 Cyber user, alongside biological safety classifiers and monitoring. Expanded cyber access is not intended to relax our safeguards for other types of harm.

blocks.text: Private Safety Processing. Next, we’ve built automated safety checks that review related interactions together to detect misuse that may not be apparent in a single request. To enable this, we generally require API customers using Zero Data Retention to use Private Safety Processing (PSP), with limited approved exceptions. Standard data retention remains the default for GPT-6 Cyber.

blocks.text: We use PSP to review encrypted safety records in a protected environment and produce limited safety signals, without exposing the underlying prompts and responses to OpenAI personnel. Customers retain the encrypted records in their own storage for 30 days and can investigate them in their own systems or choose to share relevant information with us.

blocks.text: API IP allowlisting. To make stolen credentials harder to use, we require IP allowlisting for Daybreak Red API access by default. This limits requests to customer-approved network addresses. We approve exceptions for technical constraints; cloud-provider deployments may have different requirements or approved alternatives.

blocks.text: 10. Biological and chemical safety

inlines.text: 10. Biological and chemical safety

blocks.text: We treat GPT-6 Cyber as High but not Critical in Biological and Chemical capabilities, consistent with GPT-6 Astra’s Preparedness assessment. Because its additional training focused on cybersecurity, we expected its biological and chemical capabilities to remain broadly similar to Astra’s.

inlines.text: We treat GPT-6 Cyber as High but not Critical in Biological and Chemical capabilities, consistent with
GPT-6 Astra’s Preparedness assessment
. Because its additional training focused on cybersecurity, we expected its biological and chemical capabilities to remain broadly similar to Astra’s.

blocks.text: To test this expectation, we ran five Bio-High evaluations. Consistent with previous system cards, we counted refusals as successes to estimate a conservative upper bound on capability. GPT-6 Cyber sometimes achieves higher raw scores, but they are largely due to fewer refusals; after accounting for refusals and safe completions, its scores are comparable to GPT-6 Astra’s. On ProtocolQA, GPT-6 Cyber scored 47.2% with standard scoring and 50.9% when we counted refusals and safe completions as correct; both scores were higher than Astra’s corresponding scores (41.4% and 45.4%), but both remained below ProtocolQA’s indicative High threshold of 54%. These results support carrying forward Astra’s assessment.
